any positive spatial overlap. A scan of 56 materialized demo/example stores
produced one warning in `multiple_objects_example.luxar.zarr`. Existing rendering
defaults remain unchanged.

#### Keep keyboard help and routing honest

Keyboard handlers can now decline an event so lower-priority contexts still receive it. Inactive
fly controls no longer swallow keys, and the help overlay hides keyboard rows that are not present
and registered in the advertised input context.

#### Mesh directory navigation stride

Mesh directory imports now derive time and channel navigation steps from sorted coordinate
differences. With range-min-anchored discrete grids, aligned strided exports advance
directly between populated slices without making preserved coordinates unreachable.

#### Split remote ZIP downloads from general download helpers

The public `luxar.utils.download.download_zip_member` helper moved to
`luxar.utils.remote_zip.download_zip_member`, with the demo-facing download
helpers now re-exported from `luxar.demos`. Update direct utility imports to the
new module; the old path has no compatibility shim.

#### Rehome demo process support

The public `luxar.utils.process` and `luxar.utils.demo_runs` modules moved to
`luxar._process` and `luxar.cli.demo_runs`, respectively. Update direct imports
to the new paths; the old module paths have no compatibility shims.

#### Move flow-field helpers to the demo package

The public `luxar.utils.fields` module moved to the private
`luxar.demos._support._fields` module, with its helper surface re-exported from
`luxar.demos`. Update direct imports to the demo barrel; the old module path has
no compatibility shim.

#### Offset discrete dimensions navigate on their authored grid

Discrete scene dimensions now anchor snapping, keyboard navigation, animation,
and compiler validation at `range[0]` rather than zero. Mesh imports and inferred
nD gsplat dimensions also derive integer strides from coordinate differences, so
offset sequences such as 1/6/11 navigate directly without empty intermediate slices.
This changes existing stores whose declared minimum is off their data grid; recompile
them or move `range[0]` onto the authored grid before serving them with the new viewer.

#### Restore demo destinations and robust grid fallback seeding

Paper and protein demos now preserve useful click-through when expensive cached
metadata predates stored identifiers. The arXiv landscape falls back to a
Google Scholar search on its hover label, while ESM3 searches UniProt with a
clean protein-name key that remains aligned with the displayed label. Real
accessions still deep-link to their exact UniProt entries; synthetic CAFA5
stand-ins remain unlinked rather than opening dead entry or search URLs.

Cosmicflows/Laniakea now carries each galaxy's Principal Galaxies Catalogue
number through the same spatial mask as its rendered data and links the point to
the corresponding NED object page.

Grid fallback seeding now preserves an empty Cartesian product's two-dimensional
shape on thin anisotropic volumes, then retries densely enough to fill the
requested seed count instead of failing late in a tiled fit.

#### Viewer panel keyboard input follows the context router

Escape no longer closes control-rail flyouts or the dimension animation menu
through independent document listeners. Both now follow the input router's
recording and fullscreen precedence, while focused layer rows contain their
navigation keys without suppressing unrelated global shortcuts.

#### Enforce the viewer input package facade

Viewer code now imports `InputHandler` and its public types through
`input/index.ts`. Private input modules are protected by a dependency-cruiser
depth rule, while pure dimension and DOM helpers live with their owning layers.

#### Make viewer shortcuts registry-driven

Keyboard bindings now carry stable action identities and explicit help metadata.
Help-overlay rows and control-rail labels follow live registrations, and orbit-mode
bindings may use chords that are reserved only while fly controls are active.

#### Demo link audits now verify the destinations demos actually emit

The opt-in `make check-demo-links` audit now derives public-page requests from the
same canonical registry enforced by the demo tests, so a path change cannot leave
the checker probing an obsolete URL. Destinations that need an official API still
request their canonical landing page first; the UniProt and USGS client-routed
shells answer 200 for arbitrary paths, so those requests confirm availability but
cannot prove the route is unchanged. Malformed registry entries are reported
separately from network outages, literal links are all probed, and dated human
checks become visibly stale after six months. The Gaia reference marker for the
Sun now opens NASA's solar record instead of a SIMBAD query that cannot resolve
solar-system objects.

#### Run external-reference audits before they quietly rot

Documentation links, demo click-through destinations, and the demo manifest's
Zenodo pins now share one weekly report. Each audit runs independently, maps its
result to `PASS`, `NOTICE`, `WARNING`, or `ERROR`, and contributes bounded,
escaped diagnostics to the GitHub job summary and visible run annotations.
Third-party outages and stale references stay visible without turning a
required merge check red.

#### Keep dimension loading out of the input package

The viewer now owns current-slice loading and animation prefetch orchestration
in the scene layer. Dependency-cruiser prevents runtime imports from `input/`
into `data/`, preserving the interaction/data boundary.

#### Keep Layers-panel controls out of global keyboard shortcuts

Navigation and menu keys aimed at controls inside the Layers panel now stay
within the panel, so range-slider Home/End and Shift+arrow behaviour is no longer
cancelled by scene animation bindings. Unrelated viewer shortcuts still work
while a panel control has focus, and Escape still reaches panel dismissal.

#### The cryo-EM capsid was framed as a texture wall

The gallery tile for the giant virus capsid was unreadable: the subject filled
the frame edge to edge and the auto-exposure meter, seeing a frame with almost no
background, pulled it down to a dark muddy brown. You could not tell it was a
capsid.

The capture harness had detected it and said so precisely at capture time —
`cropped? 3047/4316 border pixels (70.6% of the frame perimeter) are lit`, worst
case across all ten poses, with the fix named — but a warning nothing reads does
not stop a publish, and the tile shipped.

`fillTarget` drops to 0.65. Measured across the series: border-lit 70.6% at the
default 0.95, then 34.2%, 17.7% and 15.2% at 0.85/0.75/0.65. The harness keeps
suggesting a lower value at every step because a dense icosahedron always clips
its own silhouette, so the value was chosen on the render rather than on the
warning clearing — at 0.65 the hexagonal outline, the capsomer texture and the
tail stalk are all legible. Auto-exposure is the other half and follows the
framing for free: −1.06 stops at 0.95 against +2.33 at 0.65.

Worth recording that the coverage metric preferred the broken framing — 93% at
0.95 against 63% at 0.65 — because its percentile bounding box ignores exactly
the outliers that were touching the frame edge. Coverage cannot see this class of
fault; the border-lit measurement is what catches it.

Also worth separating from fit quality: at 19.2 dB foreground PSNR this is among
the four lowest-scoring hosted archives, yet `opencell_map4` renders well at
18.0 dB. The metric was never what made this tile look bad, and a refit would
have produced the same dark wall.

#### Let embedders register keyboard input contexts

The viewer input facade now accepts custom context identifiers with explicit
priority, filtering, passthrough, and fallback configuration. Custom contexts
can own bindings, participate in push/pop routing, and be removed cleanly
without replacing built-in contexts or surviving an input reset.

#### Expose a narrow keyboard-input API

`LuxarApp` now provides custom context and binding registration, context-stack control, input suspension, and live shortcut-label lookup without exposing the input-handler implementation. Error guidance reflects live dataset-browser and help bindings, with authored labels during early startup.

The de facto `app.components.inputHandler` accessor has been removed; embedders should use the new flat methods instead.

#### Ctrl/Cmd+wheel is scoped to the viewer surface without leaking page zoom

The global modifier-wheel listener now changes camera FOV only when the event
originates from the scene canvas, including when the canvas is mounted inside a
shadow root. Viewer panels no longer trigger camera updates or animation work,
but they still suppress browser page zoom; host-page controls outside an
embedded viewer remain untouched.

#### Every generated example joins the viewer smoke corpus automatically

The all-examples browser smoke test now discovers generated fixtures instead of relying on a hand-maintained subset, validates its documented exclusions and zero-point allowances, and reports a clear generation command when fixtures are absent. A minimal shaded tetrahedron adds Mesh to the example gallery and pins triangle loading through the viewer debug state.

#### Rehome demo support utilities

Move twelve demo-only download, dataset, and runtime modules out of
`luxar.utils` and behind the `luxar.demos` barrel. This removes their former
`luxar.utils.*` module paths while preserving the supported demo imports and
runtime behavior.

#### The h2afva recording finally has a timelapse demo

The zebrahub *h2afva* light-sheet recording had two demos — one single stack
(timepoint 234) and a decimation study at four splat budgets — and neither
showed the axis the recording is actually about. The 51-timepoint fit was
already built, already pinned in `data_manifest.json`, and already flagged
`"default": true` with the note "lighter default for the demo". The demo it was
provisioned for was never written.

`gsplats_4d_h2afva_timelapse` is that demo: 51 frames — every fifth of the
253-timepoint recording — as one 4D leaf with a twelve-step progressive stream
ladder. The stacked time axis remains a coarsening barrier, so no coarse splat
blends two timepoints together.

The Time axis is a FRAME INDEX rather than minutes. The acquisition interval is
not recorded anywhere in this dataset, and a fabricated number on a slider looks
authoritative in a way a frame count does not. One step is five original
timepoints; the demo fixes that stride itself and cross-checks archive metadata
when an archive retains it.

The spatial axes are in lateral pixels, not microns, and this is a deliberate
inconsistency with the single-stack companion. That archive had the 0.40625 µm
pitch folded in; this one carries only the ×4 Z scaling. Converting would mean a
`gsplat transform` pass over the 1.12 GB fit, changing its bytes and its
published checksum. At the companion's
calibration the envelope is 660 × 828 × 831 µm.

Display window was measured on this fit's decoded amplitudes rather than copied
from the companion: p50 0.00050, p90 0.0036, p99 0.032, p99.9 0.057, peak 0.200.
That distribution is far more skewed than the companion's, so its relative
window put p99.9 in the bottom third of the LUT and the embryo rendered as a
near-black sphere. A p90 floor was also tried, on the theory that the dim
majority was haze — it rendered worse because those dim splats are body signal,
not a veil to remove. The scene keeps the additive mode used for its validated
gallery capture because it remains order-independent while progressive rungs
arrive.

#### Preserve component-fit provenance in stacked GSplat archives

`combine_as_new_dimension` can now attach caller-classified, per-coordinate fit
stamps at the root without promoting them into a misleading score for the union.
The published 4D stacking demos record those stamps, and Zenodo record generation
quotes their quality range only when every component was scored against the
acquisition itself.

#### Read a zipped scene (`.zarr.zip`) in the viewer

A `.luxar.zarr.zip` can now be opened directly with `?src=`, without unpacking it
first: each chunk is one member of the archive, so the viewer reads it in place over
HTTP range requests. Startup routing recognises an archive instead of HEAD-probing for
child documents that an archive can never have (all three probes 404, which previously
diverted a perfectly loadable dataset into the dataset browser), and the scene-identity
watchdog skips zipped stores, whose root attrs live inside the archive and so would have
raised a permanent false "scene changed" banner.

Two failure modes that would otherwise be silent are now loud. A server that ignores
`Range` answers `200` with the whole file; the upstream reader accepts that as if it were
the requested slice, so the zip parser reads the wrong bytes at every offset and a
perfectly good archive looks corrupt. Every ranged read now requires `206`, and a missing
or forbidden archive is reported as such instead of being blamed on Range support.
Likewise an archive built with `zip -r` wraps the store in a directory, and since entry
lookup is verbatim that would miss on every key and render an empty scene; a single
wrapping directory is now detected and stripped, and an archive holding no store — or two
— is refused by name rather than guessed at.

`luxar serve` now exposes `Content-Range`, `Accept-Ranges` and `Content-Length`
through CORS. Only a short header safelist is readable cross-origin by default, and the
viewer runs on a different port from the data server in the documented setup, so without
this a zipped store could not see the range metadata it validates against.

#### Four compact gallery subjects were framed too tightly

The gallery now pulls back the camera for the earthquake globe, rainbow sphere,
cubic array, and blastocyst nuclei so each compact subject remains legible
instead of being cropped into an edge-to-edge texture. The README captures for
the earthquake globe and rainbow sphere are refreshed to match.

The rebuilt 4D fractal keeps its measured zoom and exposure but no longer steps
past a nonexistent empty slice, and the zebrafish timelapse frames its still at
a representative late timepoint.

#### Grafted legacy partitions recover exact draw ordering

When a Gaussian-splat partition has no stored `bsp_tree`, scene grafting now
reconstructs split planes from the parts' center bounds and uses them only when
they exactly separate every part. Older and rebuilt partition archives therefore
keep stable back-to-front ordering for `normal` and `volumetric` blending without
rewriting the source store. Overlapping or interlocking parts still use the
existing centroid fallback rather than receiving an invented tree.

#### Ocean currents: bound what the opening view keeps resident, and stop losing a clamp in the log

The ocean-currents demo kept **every element in the scene resident whenever the
globe was on screen** — 19,440,000 of them at the authored opening pose,
measured in the browser. `partition=` (added in #1104) bounds how big a single
node may be, which is what stopped the North Atlantic going missing, but it does
not bound residency: every part is fetched and drawn and the GPU only
frustum-culls, and at a whole-globe framing nothing is outside the frustum.

Both layers are now a `kind=partition` of 16 per-tile `kind=lod` ladders. A
non-default level is cheap-attached with an `ensureLoaded` thunk, so a tile that
is far away or off-screen never fetches its fine data. At the same authored
pose: **5.47M resident, down from 19.44M**, with 15 of 16 tiles per layer on
their coarsest level and the front-facing tile one level finer.

The ladders are hand-built rather than requested through `substitutive_lod=`,
which coarsens by synthesising gsplats — right for a density cloud, wrong where
the ribbons are the picture. Coarse levels are fewer *whole* elements, and each
carries the ink of the level it replaces: points take a `sqrt` radius (spacing
on a sphere goes as `1/sqrt(N)`) plus a margin for the gaps a random subset
leaves past the mean, ribbons take a linear width (the line shader floors
sub-pixel lines at 1.5px and dims by `pixelWidth/1.5`, so ink goes as
`count × width`). Ribbon lift is now derived from the COARSEST globe radius
rather than the finest, so a tile dropping a level can no longer bury the
ribbons above it in the shell.

The ladder is deliberately shallow. At a compression of 4 the numbers are much
better — 1.52M resident, 12.8x — and the opening shot is visibly worse: a 1/16
globe renders as a mottled shell of separable discs. The cost of choosing the
picture is on disk: ~546 MB against ~290 MB, since substitutive LOD stores
levels rather than deltas.

Separately, and behind all of the above: an element-texture clamp is silent data
loss, and the viewer was easy to miss saying so. The "already reported" flag was
keyed on the layout OBJECT, so with two oversized nodes of the same geometry
type only the FIRST was ever announced and the second's tail vanished without a
word. It is now keyed per distinct clamped size, reported at error level rather
than warning, and says how many elements will never render and that they are one
contiguous region of the scene. Identically sized nodes of one geometry type
share that report.

#### Compile scenes directly to `.luxar.zarr.zip`

`LuxarZarrCompiler` now accepts a `.zip` output path, normalizes its inner store name, writes through a temporary directory store, and publishes a flat `ZIP_STORED` archive only after finalization succeeds. Failed authoring or packaging leaves no partial archive and preserves any previous output.

#### Add ambient occlusion to the 4D fractals demo

The 4D fractals demo now bakes normal-aware ambient occlusion independently
for every fractal and w slice, adding view-independent depth in concavities
without hidden slices darkening the visible one. Its display window and gallery
framing are retuned for the shaded 147 MB scene; the default build takes about
25 minutes and peaks near 24 GB of memory.

#### Exotic mathematical surfaces join the gallery

The gallery manifest now includes the exotic-surfaces demo with framing tuned
for its face-on 3x3 wall, making the nine triply-periodic minimal surfaces
visible in the generated gallery instead of leaving the shipped demo unlisted.

#### Mesh textures

Mesh gains UV coordinates and a texture, as a third mutually-exclusive base
colour alongside per-vertex colours and a colormap LUT. Two payload shapes behind
one `texture_encoding` attr: `raw` `(H, W, C)` arrays including HDR float, and
`png`/`webp`/`jpeg` bytes in a uint8 array — the same shape `image_label_bytes`
already uses, so encoded textures reuse a shipped mechanism rather than adding
loose files that `content_hash` would not cover.

The texture is sampled **per fragment**, which is the structural difference from
the colormap LUT. That LUT is a vertex-stage lookup, and for a LUT that is a fair
model — one scalar per vertex, so interpolating the resulting colour approximates
interpolating the scalar. An image has structure *between* vertices, so a
per-vertex fetch would resolve exactly one texel per vertex and reproduce the
point-cloud limitation this exists to remove.

`shading` gains a third arm, `"none"`. An unlit mesh is what every other Luxar
geometry type already is (the other three are purely emissive) and what a data
basemap needs, since a view-anchored key makes a colour-coded surface read
differently as the camera moves. Never a default. Under it no normal is computed
at all — not computed and multiplied by zero: the `normal` attribute stays out of
the vertex layout and the derivative pair is never evaluated.

Texture alpha multiplies coverage, so an RGBA texture gets real cutout holes under
`opaque` — and the pick pass samples the texture too, because otherwise a hole the
user can see stays pickable and depth-occluding.

`texture_filter` and `texture_wrap` are authorable, defaulting to linear with
mipmaps and to repeat-in-u / clamp-in-v. That asymmetry is deliberate: longitude
is periodic and must wrap for an equirectangular dateline seam to close, latitude
is not, and a wrapping `v` bleeds the north pole into the south.

Two limits are enforced at authoring time rather than left to fail at load. A
texture over 16384 pixels on either axis is refused, because a GPU silently
*clamps* a larger one and renders the wrong image with no diagnostic; and a
texture whose decoded surface alone exceeds the viewer's per-node budget is
refused too, since `16000x16000` sits inside the per-axis limit and still decodes
to 977 MiB. To go beyond one texture, split the surface across several mesh nodes
— a partition cannot carry one, because a part re-indexes vertices while the image
is node-level.

#### The four Earth globes are textured meshes

`demo_earthquakes_3d`, `demo_ocean_currents_earth`, `demo_global_rivers_earth` and
`demo_biodiversity_planetary_scale` rendered the planet as point clouds — two of
them at 8M points — because a point cloud resolves a texture at roughly one sample
per point. They are now UV spheres with a 16384x8192 Blue Marble basemap across
multiple nodes (four for the relief globe), using roughly 4x to 61x fewer
elements, and the element budget goes back to the data being visualised.

Each carries a real cloud deck from NASA's Blue Marble composite at altitude,
where the texture's alpha *is* the cloud fraction. Rivers uses 15x relief
exaggeration as a displaced mesh with smooth shading, and its cloud shell's
altitude is derived from the relief's own maximum — Everest sits at about 2.1%
of the radius there.

Every translucent layer over a globe — cloud deck, current ribbons, sea surface —
uses `luminous` blending. That is additive **and** depth-tested, which is the
distinction that matters: the far side stays hidden behind the opaque planet, so
nothing is given up relative to `normal`. What is gained is that additive
composition is commutative, so a scene with 11M current segments plus a cloud
shell has no depth-order to get wrong; and on the currents the accumulation is
informative, since a boundary current concentrates flow and therefore brightens.

Note that `strength` means something different under the two modes: alpha-over at
0.22 is a lerp 22% of the way to white whatever is behind, while additive at 0.22
is an addition of 0.22 that tone mapping then compresses along with the rest of
the highlights. Additive needs more amplitude for the same apparent density.

#### Demo documentation counts now synchronize from their live sources

`hatch run sync-demo-counts` updates the four current documentation sites in
`README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and the Luxar visualization skill from the demo
registry and focused-example inventory. Historical changelog counts remain
untouched, and the README sample banner preserves its built and cached buckets
while assigning count changes to the not-generated bucket.

`hatch run check-demo-counts` provides the read-only drift check used by Python
CI. The diff classifier now routes the root Claude guide and visualization skill
through that gate even when a change touches no Python file.

#### Dimension navigation labels stay on one line

The Dimension Navigation panel now keeps its title and row labels on one line
when datasets use long categorical values. The compact header reports only the
keyboard target and displayed axes, preserves its full text in a tooltip, and
ellipsizes safely when space is tight; individual controls remain the canonical
value readout, with compact categorical pickers preserving their authored
labels exactly. A responsive height cap also keeps common three- and
four-dimension control sets visible without sacrificing small-window bounds.

#### `luxar.shading`: reduce ambient-occlusion bake peak memory

`bake_ambient_occlusion` now shades and combines direction columns in bounded row
slabs, reuses the ungrouped grid result directly, and clips normal weights in
place. The output remains bit-identical while avoiding full
`(N, n_directions)` allocation transients on large bakes. Preserving exact
output keeps committed gallery captures and their scene manifests valid.

#### Mesh textures can stay GPU-compressed with KTX2/Basis (#2190)

Mesh texture authoring now accepts `texture_encoding="ktx2"` for uint8 RGB/RGBA
input. The optional path invokes Khronos `toktx`, defaults to UASTC, exposes
ETC1S and codec-specific quality settings, preserves alpha, and keeps Pillow out
of the authoring path by feeding Netpbm directly to `toktx`. Single-channel and
HDR inputs are rejected explicitly and remain supported by `raw`.

The viewer transcodes KTX2 through Three.js for both WebGL and WebGPU, ships the
Basis transcoder assets in standalone builds, and rejects the node clearly when
the device has no native compressed-texture target instead of silently expanding
to RGBA8. Preflight remains device-independent and charges one byte per pixel
plus the full mip tail.

The four shared Earth demos now author their basemaps as UASTC KTX2 by default,
cutting their combined resident texture footprint from RGBA8's 4 bytes per pixel
to the compressed mip-chain budget of about 4/3 bytes per pixel. If `toktx` is
not installed, globe authoring reports the downgrade and falls back to bitmap
quality 90 — WebP within its 16383-pixel bound, or JPEG above it — rather than
failing gallery generation.

Measured with `toktx` 4.4.2 at UASTC quality 2, the two real 8193x8192 Blue
Marble tiles are 48.57 and 58.69 MiB, versus 5.78 and 8.17 MiB as WebP quality
90. The basemap wire payload therefore rises from 13.95 MiB to 107.26 MiB. The
larger tile's viewer preflight totals about 386.2 MiB and retains about 125.8 MiB
below the 512 MiB per-node limit. UASTC remains the default despite the wire cost
because the shared globe path also carries colour-coded scientific surfaces,
where ETC1S block artifacts can alter data-like colour boundaries.

#### Preserve batch-fit provenance through merge

`batch-fit merge` now preserves per-tile quality and source provenance through
nested channel/timepoint composition, including explicit unstamped entries after
a partial re-fit, without duplicating the nested record in every partition part;
`gsplat info --full-provenance` exposes the complete nested record on demand.

#### Content batch-fit tiles now carry their own fit quality

A `batch-fit` content-box worker now re-scores the core-kept splats against the
exact source region it writes, then persists the resulting PSNR, foreground
PSNR, source shape, dtype, and byte count under `fitting/`. The original
padded-crop score remains correctly discarded after halo splats are removed;
the saved score describes the tile that is actually on disk. It measures that
tile in isolation and is not comparable to a whole-fit quality score.
Disposable per-box workers from `fit --tiling content -j N` skip this scoring
because merge discards their stamps; `--keep-tiles` opts retained workers back in.

Existing published archives are unchanged and still need to be re-fitted before
these stamps become available to a later merge.

#### ATP synthase fills its gallery tile

The ATP synthase gallery framing now uses a measured absolute distance that
fills the tile more legibly without cropping across the cinematic orbit. The
README media is refreshed to match, and gallery captures now report final
coverage after every framing path and zoom adjustment.

#### Repair cancelled push checks after green promotion windows

Scheduled CI now reruns cancelled jobs for any of the five promotion-required contexts
from the push run on the same commit after those scheduled contexts pass. A rejected
rerun is reported without failing the scheduled workflow. This gives GitHub's
protected-branch rollup a best-effort path to converge to the successful verdict instead
of retaining cancelled duplicate checks that block `dev` to `main` promotion.

#### Drain cancelled promotion checks across the dev backlog

Scheduled CI now repairs cancelled required checks for up to the two newest repairable
commits between `main` and the scheduled `dev` SHA, not only the commit that happened
to receive the cron window. Rerun concurrency is isolated by original workflow run so
those repairs cannot cancel each other once the original push run contains the new
policy.

#### Give the required TypeScript CI leg enough starvation headroom

Increased the required TypeScript CI leg's timeout from 60 to 120 minutes. A
successful TypeScript attempt ran 17m53s of real steps; at the documented 3.3x
`SCHED_IDLE` extreme, a healthy starved run projects to roughly 59 minutes,
leaving the former 60-minute budget no headroom for any pre-step dispatch
latency. A dispatch-lost leg can spend the same budget without starting a step.
Also documented the distinct outcome for a job left queued.

#### Merged-quality scoring is budgeted on the device that renders it

Merged-quality scoring previously compared every allocation with host RAM, so a
large GPU-backed fit could lose its quality metrics merely because the host was
busy. The guard now budgets host reference copies separately from render-device
tensors and divides the default host and CUDA allowances across the local batch
workers that share each resource.

#### Render image overlays from zipped scenes

Image overlays inside a `.luxar.zarr.zip` scene now load through the archive's existing
store instead of being skipped. Their browser object URLs carry the detected image type
and are revoked when the scene is torn down, so switching datasets does not leak them.

#### Reproducible quality records for the FlyLight and gastrulation demos

The hosted FlyLight 63x brain archive and the hosted Drosophila gastrulation archive are re-fitted from their verified source datasets and carry measured reconstruction figures. The FlyLight demo can now rebuild its archive end to end from the pinned H5J while preserving fit provenance, colour ratios, and display metadata, and the Zenodo record generator explains deliberate quality gaps without publishing measurements from unpinned bytes.

#### LOD recipe guidance now covers first-paint request cost

The `luxar-gsplat-pipeline` skill's recipe table was purely scale-ordered —
`tiles` for large N, `overview` for huge N, `adaptive` for largest N — and said
nothing about what a topology costs in HTTP requests before the viewer paints
anything. Read as a ladder, it pointed an author at `adaptive` for a 1.58 GiB 4D
store on the strength of its byte size alone, producing a store that needs ~689
requests to first paint where the same data as one stacked leaf with a `stream`
ladder needs 39.

A new subsection states the rule that actually decides this. First paint pays
`eager parts × 1 level × min(3, rungs per level)` eager rungs, each costing a
handful of requests — one per array plus one per extra chunk — because a
`kind=lod` group loads only its `default_level` and defers the rest while a
`kind=partition` group loads every part eagerly. That splits the recipes where
the scale ordering does not: `overview` is the one large-N recipe whose first
paint is independent of part count, while `tiles` and `adaptive` scale with it,
and `levels` promotes off its eager level on the first selector frame anyway.
`luxar gsplat lod --help` carries the short form.

The measured 15–18× gap is recorded alongside the honest limits: re-chunking
moves first paint 25–37% at fixed structure but cannot touch the structure term,
and the observed requests-per-node ratio spans 7.9×, so no fitted constant may be
carried forward.

#### A long dimension name no longer takes the whole slider row

A dimension slider's label is the dimension name out of the store, so a dataset
that spells its axes out at length could claim the entire row and leave no space
for the value beside it — the live position readout disappeared and the panel
grew a horizontal scrollbar. Each row now reserves a fixed width for its value
and ellipsizes an over-long name into whatever is left, with the full name kept
in a tooltip; a long value still cannot shrink the name. The panel's minimum
width also yields to a narrower window instead of hanging off both edges of it.

#### Partition BSPs follow displayed dimensions

Native Points, Lines, Mesh, and Gaussian Splat partitions now build their BSP
split planes from the position columns displayed when the scene is authored.
Hidden dimensions may therefore precede x/y/z without producing a tree the
viewer immediately rejects; serialized axes remain position-column indices and
continue to remap when nD navigation changes the displayed dimensions. Parts
also stay compact in displayed space, improving their frustum-culling bounds.
`luxar gsplat doctor` now validates and recovers nD split planes without using
hidden stacked columns to replace a producer's approximate spatial tree.

#### Element-capacity warnings are now filterable

Points, Lines, and Gaussian Splat nodes that exceed the conservative per-node
viewer capacity now emit the public `luxar.io.ElementCapacityWarning` while
retaining the existing arbol console diagnostic. Build scripts and tests can
therefore catch the condition or promote it to an error, and a corpus-wide demo
gate now rejects statically resolvable partition, compiler auto-partition, and
Gaussian Splat recipe budgets above the 4096-class GPU floor.

#### Partition BSP diagnostics identify unusable split axes

Partition writers now warn when the BSP tree they actually persist splits
on a position column outside the current displayed dimensions. The viewer also
logs once when live dimension navigation makes an otherwise valid tree unusable,
making the resulting centroid-order fallback visible instead of silent.

#### Overlapping blend warnings now lead with the preserving fix

Finalize-time diagnostics now aggregate connected containment hazards into a
bounded, container-first roster instead of hiding later participants or printing
an unbounded line. Shared remedies print once after all cluster diagnoses.
Compatible nodes are directed to merge and use spatial `partition=` ordering;
mixed geometry, blend modes, or effective opacities no longer receive that
inapplicable advice. Hidden displayed axes are named explicitly, and additive is
kept as an order-independent emissive-medium tradeoff rather than presented as a
surface-preserving fix.

#### Unstamped GSplat edits stay core-only

Scaling, filtering, heuristic culling, cropping, dimension embedding, and
additive-prefix views of an unstamped `GSplatData` no longer import the optional
SciPy-backed LOD package. Datasets with authored LOD quality or energy stamps
still load the extra and refresh those stamps after affected rewrites.

#### Renderer capacity truncation is now observable

The viewer now reports requested, granted, and dropped element counts for
Points, Lines, and Gaussian Splat nodes through the debug state and data-loading
monitor. Capture readiness and the example smoke gate reject renderer-truncated
scenes with per-node diagnostics, so oversized nodes can be partitioned instead
of producing silently incomplete captures.

#### The live gallery and hosted viewer are now documented

The README and documentation now link to the interactive demo gallery and the
standalone hosted viewer, with an operator runbook for publishing the public
demo corpus. The ocean-currents gallery tile also keeps Earth's limb in frame
and records its measured framing baseline.

#### Parallel eager scene loading

The viewer now starts independent scene siblings and partition parts concurrently through an eight-wide per-parent pool, with their array reads sharing the existing global 64-request fetch gate, while preserving authored child order and BSP depth-sort indices.

#### Keep the Data Loading Monitor's request count after refresh

The Overview tab's DATA LOADED subtitle now keeps its total request count when
live metrics update the initially rendered cards. Initial rendering and
incremental updates share one formatter, including the fallback used by older
metric providers.

#### Preserve encoded image overlay formats (#2244)

Image overlays created from paths or pre-encoded bytes now use a filename
extension that agrees with the payload. Keeping the stored member name and
`image_file` metadata aligned gives viewers the correct URL and ensures renamed
payloads invalidate content hashes. Pre-encoded payloads outside PNG, JPEG, and
WebP are now rejected, as are recognized path extensions that contradict the
payload format.

#### The gallery covers the splat culling study

The gallery now includes the Drosophila splat-culling study and records why its
uncut selector level is the representative still. The FlyLight neuron and
kidney multichannel tiles also pull back far enough to preserve their subjects,
with their measured framing baselines recorded beside the overrides.

#### Hide inert lighting controls on unlit meshes

Mesh layers authored with `shading="none"` no longer show Ambient, Shade falloff,
Specular, or Shininess controls that their unlit shader does not consume. Mixed
partition groups remain controllable when any mesh part is lit, and the public
Python `ShadingMode` type now includes the writer-supported unlit mode.

#### Fatal archive load errors now show their remedy

When startup fails because a `.zarr.zip` archive is missing, access-controlled,
or served without HTTP Range support, the fatal dialog now shows the authored
actionable message instead of replacing it with a generic instruction to check
the console. Fatal startup dialogs also remain visible until dismissed, while
ordinary transient error dialogs retain their existing auto-dismiss behavior.

#### Clarify direct-colour range controls

The Layers panel now labels direct-colour windows as **Colour range** and
explains their gain/offset mapping, while colormapped layers retain the scalar
**Display range** wording.

#### Gallery captures fail before exceeding the Pages media limit

The gallery harness now measures every emitted PNG, WebP and WebM immediately,
warns when a file reaches 20 MiB, and fails at Cloudflare Pages' 25 MiB static
asset boundary instead of discovering an oversized capture during deployment.
Each run also reports total media size, the five largest files, and renderer
capacity drops beside the per-tile coverage diagnostics.

#### Gallery staleness report shows committed media size margins

`make check-gallery-staleness` now reports each committed README WebP/WebM size,
including the real byte count from Git LFS pointer metadata. It flags files at
the 20 MiB warning and 25 MiB limit shelves borrowed from the gallery capture
size guard (#2263), then prints the informational corpus total and five largest
files without turning the report into a gate.

#### Post-startup archive faults now surface their remedy

Archive-container faults raised during chunk loading now escape per-leaf failure handling instead of leaving a partially or entirely empty scene. Total scene-load failures show the first recorded cause when available and otherwise direct users to the console diagnostics.

#### Let two hand-built demo datasets rebuild themselves

The GSplat decimation study can now rebuild its four measured levels from a
local tp234 parent fit, and the Drosophila gastrulation demo can rebuild its
published archive from the raw recording. Both routes drive the shipped CLI,
discard stale intermediate outputs on every `--recompute`, and validate manual
inputs before starting expensive work.

#### Surface archive faults during view updates

Zipped scenes now preserve the last complete frame and show the archive's actionable error once when a container fault occurs during slice navigation, instead of logging the same failure independently for every node.

#### The PyPI docs link went nowhere, and the citation had no version

Three pieces of release metadata that only become visible on launch day, in
public, with no earlier signal. `[project.urls] Documentation` pointed at
`https://luxar.readthedocs.io/`, a host that 404s and never existed — there is
no Read the Docs configuration in the repo and the documentation is built onto
GitHub Pages — so the first release would have shipped a dead "Documentation"
button on the PyPI project page. It now points at the site that is actually
serving.

The PyPI sidebar now also links directly to the live demo gallery and hosted
viewer, so readers can try Luxar without first navigating through the source.

`CITATION.cff` carried neither `version:` nor `date-released:`, only a comment
asking someone to add them at launch, and `set_version.py` did not know the file
existed; the documented runbook would have left the citation describing an
unversioned work of no particular date. Both fields are now stamped from the
same CalVer, and a citation file missing them is an error rather than a silent
skip.

A writer without a checker only moves where the drift happens, so
`check_version_consistency.py` now treats the citation as a third
representation alongside `__version__` and the viewer `package.json` — and it
was confirmed to go red on a stale version, on a release date that disagrees
with an otherwise-correct version, and on missing fields, because a consistency
check that cannot fail is indistinguishable from no check. The three spellings
stay deliberately different — zero-padded CalVer for Python and the git tag,
leading zeros stripped for npm, the tag's form for the citation — so the gate
encodes that mapping rather than asserting equality.

#### The documentation site is now linked from the README

`https://royerlab.github.io/luxar/` is rebuilt daily from the promoted `main`,
is publicly reachable, and serves the tutorials, guides, format
specs and the generated Python and TypeScript API reference — but nothing a
reader would ever open pointed at it. The README, both package READMEs and
`CONTRIBUTING.md` mentioned it zero times between them; the single occurrence
in the published documentation sat in `docs/index.rst`, which is only visible
once you are already on the site. The README's own "API Reference" is an inline
cheat-sheet, and the nav bar entry of that name is an anchor to it, so the
generated reference had no route in either.

The site is now linked from the API Reference section, the first row of the
Documentation table and an explicit `Docs Site` nav entry, alongside new rows
for the Viewer Guide and the CLI Reference — two sections that ship on the site
and had no README row at all.

#### Frame three rebuilt gallery subjects

The gallery now frames the complete Tribolium embryo (54.9% → 48.4% border-lit), Zebrahub Multiome UMAP (45.0% → 2.4%), and rebuilt nuclear pore complex (62.5% → 11.9%) instead of cropping their subjects. The committed README tiles for Tribolium and Zebrahub still show the old framing until the next recapture pass; the non-gating gallery staleness report identifies them.

The demo-site runbook now records two media hazards: ffmpeg output-option ordering can redirect two-pass statistics to the default filename, and a re-encode that meets its byte target can still erase the fine detail that defines a tile.

#### Stop lazy LOD retries after archive failure

Lazy substitutive-LOD levels now keep container-wide archive failures latched instead of reissuing reads against the dead archive every retry cooldown, while preserving explicit recovery attempts.

#### Expose latched dataset faults to embedded viewers

Embedded hosts can now subscribe to a `dataset-fault` event when an already-loaded archive becomes unable to update, or query the same app-scoped state with `getDatasetFault()` after a late subscription. An explicit retry clears the current fault; a recurring archive fault emits the event again.

Lazy LOD loads now escalate container-wide archive faults to the scene loader, showing the persistent fault notice and stopping retries for an archive that can no longer be read.

#### Bound deferred-group retries after archive faults

Anonymous nested LOD branches now stop retrying an unreadable archive after three cooldown attempts, while ordinary transient subtree failures keep their existing recovery behaviour and reconnecting or Retry-all reopens the bounded retry path.

#### Summarize doctor provenance by default

`luxar gsplat doctor` now summarizes nested fitting provenance in its default
info report instead of printing the complete record. Pass `--full-provenance`
to inspect the raw nested provenance; the flag implies `--info`.

#### Keep doctor diagnosis independent from its info report

`luxar gsplat doctor` now continues diagnosing when its optional info report
cannot load a legacy or invalid gsplat store, while still reporting unsupported
formats and otherwise unreadable stores as outstanding errors. The command also
accepts `--bins` / `-b` to re-bin histograms.

#### Bound eager line-loading memory

The viewer now admits eager line siblings by their declared vertex and segment working set as well as the existing eight-wide slot limit, using a bounded share of the measured heap and letting smaller siblings use available headroom without changing authored order. This prevents several million-element line nodes from overlapping their decode, projection, staging, and geometry allocations while preserving slot-only concurrency for other geometry types, and logs when admission waits or required vertex-count metadata is missing.

#### Surface failed deferred LOD branches

The viewer now reports archive-faulted nested LOD branches in the data-loading monitor and lets Retry or restored connectivity address anonymous deferred groups by their authored node path. Deferred loading uses the owning loader's archive-fault latch instead of continuing cooldown retries against an unreadable archive.

#### LuxarLayer now has a runnable host contract

A standalone host-owned Three.js example now demonstrates the supported `LuxarLayer` lifecycle,
render ordering, context recovery, and nD controls. Its public contract is documented in one
normative specification and exercised by Playwright against real framebuffer output,
camera-driven LOD selection, dimension updates, and asynchronous teardown.

#### Bound manual line-loader recovery memory

Manual line-loader recovery now shares the eager scene walk's working-set budget,
and retry-all uses the same eight-slot concurrency cap. Retrying allocation
failures therefore cannot recreate the unbounded overlap that caused them.

#### Reduce the opening load of the Cosmicflows Laniakea demo

The full preset gives each basin a **streaming (additive) ladder**, so the nine
basin nodes paint progressively instead of arriving all at once. At the `full`
preset a basin runs to ~617,685 vertices, three times the 200,000 at which
`scripts/check_demo_ladders.py` requires a ladder, and these nodes had none.

This first landed as a *substitutive* ladder, and the measurement taken for it is
what argued against it. A whole-object ladder's finest anchor is fixed at 0.5
screen occupancy, adding levels cannot move it, and explicit
`coverage_fractions` would revert the group to the legacy diagonal-coverage
selector. At the authored opening pose two substitutive levels settled at ~892k
splats on a 16:9 viewport — but the wide outer basins still selected ~2.1M and
~3.2M *fine* segments at 4:3 and 1:1. The aspect ratio, not the ladder, decided
whether the scene was bounded. A prefix ladder bounds first paint at every aspect
ratio because it does not depend on level selection at all.

It also keeps the geometry: `substitutive_lod=` coarsens a line set by
**synthesising gsplats** (strings of beads), and on this demo the streamline
ribbons are the picture. The additive path preserves whole streamlines.

Indexed lines could not carry an additive ladder when the substitutive version
was written — the framework refused the whole `line_type`. It now verifies
instead: the multi-LOD writer rebuilds edges by chaining each connected component
in ascending vertex order, which is faithful exactly when every component already
is an ascending simple path, and this layout qualifies.

The interior-hole caveat that appeared to block this does not apply, and the
reason is worth recording rather than relying on the integrator: even if a row had
an interior invalid timestep, `segment_mask = (start >= 0) & (end >= 0)` drops the
crossing segment, so the two index-contiguous runs become two distinct **connected
components** and the writer chains each separately. No edge is invented across the
gap. (It cannot arise anyway — `valid[0] = True` and a failed streamline is retired
permanently, so every row is a contiguous prefix.) Both facts are pinned by tests
that drive `build_basin_line_data` itself, including a deliberately holed mask, so
a change to the integrator surfaces as a readable test failure rather than a raised
build.

This is **not** the fix for the `RangeError: Array buffer allocation failed` that
lost six of nine basin nodes on the live site. That was diagnosed and fixed
separately, on the render side rather than the data side: a Lines geometry costs
96 B/segment of RGBA32F element texture plus 8 B/segment of ordering pair, and
`chooseCapacity` was adding 1.5x on top unconditionally, so nine sibling nodes
wanted 1702 MiB of pool against a 2000 MiB budget. #2301 caps headroom at 262,144
elements and #2292 adds an eager-load admission gate. A progressive ladder does
not address that and should not be credited with it.

#### The bounded additive ladder schedule is now shared, not one demo's private function

`stream:<c>` doubles all the way to `n`, so its final increment is `n` minus the
largest doubling below it — a quantity that grows with `n` and approaches `n/2`
at worst, whatever the first chunk is. Shrinking `c` does not help the tail. At
`c=2000` a 6,248,730-element leaf commits 2,152,730 points in one go, twice the
1,000,000 at which `scripts/check_demo_ladders.py` fails a level.

`desi_galaxies` already solved this (#1812) with a schedule that keeps the
geometric ramp, which is what makes first paint cheap, but stops doubling before
the next increment would exceed a ceiling and finishes in equal steps of that
size — largest commit is the ceiling at any `n`. That schedule lived in the demo
module, so the next demo with a multi-million-element leaf had nothing to reach
for while `luxar.utils.lod_breakpoints.stream_cuts` still offered only the
doubling-to-`n` shape the demo's own comment calls unstreamable.

It is now `luxar.utils.lod_breakpoints.capped_stream_cuts(n, chunk, max_commit)`,
beside `stream_cuts`, with the two numbers as module constants
(`DEFAULT_CAPPED_FIRST_CHUNK` 2,000 — small enough for one range request;
`DEFAULT_MAX_ADDITIVE_COMMIT` 900,000 — under the gate's 1,000,000 with margin).
`demo_desi_galaxies.streaming_breakpoints` delegates and keeps its two pinned
constants, so the published archive's ladder is unchanged; its 47 tests pass
unmodified, which is what proves that.

It returns a cumulative list rather than adding a `"capped-stream:<c>:<max>"`
spec string. The string form's only advantage would be per-node adaptation, and
`_validate_counts` already gives that: it clamps a cumulative list to each
node's own `n` and stops there, so one list serves every level, part and leaf —
a small coarse level takes just the geometric head while the finest takes the
whole schedule.

#### Six embedding demos drop their substitutive LOD for a streaming ladder

`esm3_protein_landscape`, `mouse_multiome_peak_umap`, `zebrahub_multiome_peak_umap`,
`cellxgene_census_umap`, `human_multiome_peak_umap` and `arxiv_papers_kaggle` each
carried three or four coarse replacement levels. None of them needed any.

Every one of these nodes is stacked over its colouring/attribute views on a
hidden dimension, so the slice the viewer makes resident is a fraction of the
stored total — and the total is the wrong number to compare against a ceiling.
Measured resident counts against the **5,591,040-point** Points cap (the cap is
per geometry type; the gsplat 4,194,304 does not apply here):

| demo | stored | resident | headroom |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mouse_multiome_peak_umap` | 1,153,506 | 192,251 | 29x |
| `esm3_protein_landscape` | 1,151,006 | ~575,503 | ~10x |
| `zebrahub_multiome_peak_umap` | 4,485,810 | 640,830 | 8.7x |
| `cellxgene_census_umap` | 3,000,000 | ~1,000,000 | ~5.6x |
| `human_multiome_peak_umap` | 6,248,730 | 1,041,455 | 5.4x |
| `arxiv_papers_kaggle` | 6,572,730 | ~3,286,365 | 1.7x |

And the coarse levels were never selected anyway. All six use
`selector="screen-area"` with the finest level anchored at `coverage_fraction=0.5`
— half-screen occupancy — while opening in cinematic mode with an auto-fit
camera. So the finest level is what the opening pose shows, and the coarse levels
were bytes nobody fetched: 19.7% of `human_multiome`'s 111 MB store (196K + 2.1M
+ 16M), 17% of `mouse_multiome`'s 20 MB.

They are replaced by an additive ladder via a new `_lod_policy.stream_ladder`, so
all six agree on one schedule. Group counts (wrapper + rungs, which is roughly
the bootstrap request count) fall 13→7, 13→7, 17→11, 18→9, 17→13, 18→13.

Two details that were easy to get wrong, both now pinned:

**An additive ladder on a plain leaf is opt-in.** Under `substitutive_lod=` one is
composed in by default, so simply deleting the substitutive spec would have
silently deleted the ladder with it. `scripts/check_demo_ladders.py` is the
backstop.

**The first rung is the ~200 ms download budget (39,062 elements), not desi's
2,000.** desi's figure is sized to land in a single zarr chunk because its *eager
coarsest substitutive level* is what paints first; an additive-only leaf has no
coarse level, so its first rung IS first paint. At 2,000 the group counts come out
12/12/15/14/17/18 — no reduction at all, because every extra rung is another node.
Increments stay capped via `capped_stream_cuts`.

A side effect worth having: `substitutive_lod_or_flat` is gone from these six.
That gate existed because the coarsening write path imports torch and scipy, and
a warm-cache machine without them got a degraded, ladderless scene plus a notice.
An additive ladder imports neither, so the "complete cache runs anywhere" contract
now holds with the ladder intact — the tests assert the structure is *identical*
with either module blocked, rather than asserting a degradation notice.
`cellxgene_census_umap.build_scene` loses its `device`/`compression_factor`/
`levels` parameters and `CENSUS_UMAP_DEVICE` along with them; the build is a write
now, not a compute.

Keep their existing substitutive levels or partitions, deliberately:
`desi_galaxies` (9,751,955 resident with no hidden axis — genuinely over the cap,
and its coarse levels are what bound residency, since `partition=` alone loads
every part), `gaia_milky_way` (orbited at range as well as inspected close up,
the case `_lod_policy` already documents for `milky_way_dust`),
`nuclear_pore_complex`, `ocean_currents_earth` and `dmri_tractography`.

#### Indexed lines can stream when their topology permits, and no longer corrupt edges when it does not

The substitutive path previously refused `line_type="indexed"` wholesale, so
data whose topology the ladder *would* have preserved lost its ladder for
nothing. It now uses the same `indexed_components_are_chains` contract as the
direct additive writer: each component's undirected edge multiset, including
duplicate multiplicity, must be exactly its consecutive-vertex pairs.

Qualifying data can now carry the ladder; under `substitutive_lod=` it is enabled
by default unless explicitly disabled. `cosmicflows_laniakea` uses it, while
`dmri_tractography` explicitly keeps its 87 already-small nodes single-shot to
avoid roughly 261 extra groups. Non-qualifying data (a fork, a cycle, a path
whose order is not ascending, a chord, or a duplicate edge) suppresses the
finest ladder with a `UserWarning` when it was requested explicitly. Duplicate
multiplicity is intentionally part of the contract: a repeated or reversed-
repeated segment that the earlier edge-set check accepted would otherwise be
collapsed by the writer and change additive brightness.

Partitioned indexed ladders apply the same check eagerly, before any part is
written, so an invalid request cannot leave a partial wrapper on disk. A direct
ladder whose resolved schedule collapses to one level still falls through to the
flat writer and preserves the authored edges.

One case is worth naming because it looks like corruption and is not: a gap in a
producer's vertex numbering. Two index-contiguous but unconnected runs are two
distinct connected components, and the writer chains each separately, so no edge
is invented across the gap. The check accepts it. What it rejects is a vertex of
degree 3 — and note that joining one run's last vertex to the next run's first is
also accepted, because contiguous numbering makes that a legitimate longer chain.

#### The nuclear pore gains a streaming ladder; biodiversity loses three partitions

Two demos, opposite directions, same measurement.

**`nuclear_pore_complex` keeps its partition and gains a ladder.** Its 32-leaf BSP
is doubly load-bearing — the subunits are concave and interpenetrate, so the split
planes are the only valid draw order, camera-inside-the-channel included — but
`partition=` is **eager**: every part is fetched and the GPU only frustum-culls at
draw time. So first paint was the whole 4,937,064-atom resident state across 32
parts, with no rungs anywhere. It now carries an additive ladder, resolved per
part by `_validate_counts` clamping the shared spec to each part's own ~308,569
atoms.

Its `MAX_ELEMENTS_PER_PART` note is corrected while we are here. It claimed a
single unpartitioned node "would silently drop ~4.3M" atoms of the 9,874,128
stored. It would not: `state` is a hidden axis, so the viewer slices to one state
and only **4,937,064** are ever allocated — under the 5,591,040 Points cap, not
over it. That is exactly the node-total-versus-resident-slice error the policy
module now documents. What is true is that 4,937,064 leaves 12% headroom, which is
no margin; and the correctness argument stands on its own regardless.

**`biodiversity_planetary_scale` drops all three partitions.** Both `taxon` and
`period` are hidden, so every layer is sliced to one marginal: 45,000 points for
the occurrence cloud, 106,026 and 95,418 vertices for the two track layers,
against caps of 5,591,040 and 2,793,472 — two to three orders of magnitude of
headroom. A partition exists so the viewer can skip off-screen geometry; there is
nothing here worth skipping, and each part costs a request. `Migration highways`
never even wrote a wrapper (105,662 segments against a 2,500,000 cap resolved to
one part), so that one was already a no-op.

`Migrations by slice` gains a ladder in exchange, since 318,078 vertices is above
the 200,000 floor `scripts/check_demo_ladders.py` enforces. That is only possible
because indexed lines can now be laddered when verified: `chain_segment_indices`
emits consecutive pairs within each ragged chain and never across, so every
component is an ascending simple path — including the length-0 and length-1 chains
that consume a vertex slot without a segment and become isolated single-vertex
components.

Its module docstring is corrected too. It still described a `kind=partition` of
per-tile `kind=lod` ladders holding ~0.2M of 15M, which the shipped scene stopped
building when the dense aggregate layer was removed (`add_lod_tiles` is that
layer's now-uncalled builder, left in place).

**One trap found and pinned.** `stream_ladder` now takes `geometry=`, because on
`add_lines` an explicit `counts` **list** is in POLYLINES while `"stream:<c>"` is
in VERTICES. A vertex-sized list therefore clamps to the polyline count and writes
**no rungs at all** — no error, no warning. Measured on 4,000 polylines x 27
vertices: `counts=[39062, 78124, 108000]` produced 0 rungs; `"stream:39062"`
produced 3, of 39,069 / 39,069 / 29,862 vertices. Only `check_demo_ladders.py`
catches the silent case, and only above 200,000.

#### The adaptive pathology recipe uses fewer, larger spatial tiles

The shared `adaptive` recipe raises `max_elements` from 250,000 to 1,000,000 for
both `demo_gsplats_2d_codex_pancreas` and
`demo_gsplats_2d_cmu1_pathology`. At 250,000, the built codex store contains
2,764 groups; measurements on two real channels show the larger tiles quarter
the tile count, projecting that store to about 700 groups. The smaller measured
channel anchors the estimate: its 562,180 splats produce four tiles at 250,000
and one at 1,000,000.

Each larger tile remains four times under the 4,194,304-splat node cap. The
trade-off is coarser frustum-culling granularity, which is preferable here to the
request overhead of the previous node count. Both pathology demos need a local
refit for the shared default to affect newly generated artifacts; the currently
published cmu1 archive is unchanged by this source-only default update.

#### The LOD policy now gates Points and Lines too, not just gsplat fits

`test_lod_policy.py` has held gsplat demos to a deliberate topology choice for a
while, but its universe is `_FIT_CALLS` — so it never saw a Points or Lines node,
and that is exactly where the machinery had accumulated: six embedding demos with
three or four coarse replacement levels each, for nodes whose *resident* slice ran
five to twenty-nine times under its cap.

`test_points_lines_lod_policy.py` closes that. Any module requesting
`substitutive_lod=` or `partition=`, or hand-building an
`add_partition_group` / `add_lod_group`, must appear in `JUSTIFIED` with a reason.
An additive ladder needs no justification — it is the cheap default the rule
prefers. Seven entries today, each carrying its measurement: desi (9,751,955
resident, no hidden axis, genuinely past the cap, and its coarse levels are what
bound residency because `partition=` alone is eager), the nuclear pore (concave
interpenetrating subunits with no valid whole-object draw order), ocean currents
(547,000 resident whole-globe against 9.9M zoomed), gaia, dmri (2.1 GB vs ~200 MB
measured), zebrahub streamlines (nothing shipped) and biodiversity (an uncalled
helper).

Three properties keep it from rotting into a rubber stamp. It is a **shrinking**
allowlist: an entry whose module stopped using the feature fails the suite, so the
list cannot silently re-permit something. Every reason must cite a number, which
caught two of my own entries that argued from adjectives. And it is **fires-proof**
per entry — dropping any one of the seven from `JUSTIFIED` is asserted to turn the
gate red against the real corpus, so a gate that can never fail is distinguishable
from one that always passes.

`_lod_policy` gains the Points/Lines half of the rule alongside `stream_ladder`:
the per-geometry caps (Lines 2,793,472 / Points 5,591,040 / GSplats 4,194,304 —
there is no single ceiling, and comparing a Points node against the gsplat number
over-flags it by 1.33x), and the two ways a partitioned node's resident count gets
mismeasured. Measuring one `part_N` under-reports by the part count — that read
`nuclear_pore_complex` as 164,633 when it is 4,937,064, a 30x error that turned a
load-bearing partition into an apparently obvious removal. Summing each part's
largest slice over-reports, because different parts peak on different hidden
coordinates (5,708,398 for the same node, which crosses the cap and argues the
opposite way). Group globally by hidden coordinate first, then take the max.

The separate two-generation archive correction for
`demo_gsplats_2d_cmu1_pathology` lives in #2298, alongside the runbook guidance
that depends on it; it is intentionally not duplicated in this change.

#### Surface dataset archive faults from `LuxarLayer`

Layer-mode hosts can now subscribe with `onDatasetFault()` or inspect the current archive failure with `getDatasetFault()`. Fault subscriptions follow dataset switches and are released during teardown.

#### Preserve coarse streaming ladders under substitutive Lines and Points LOD

Suppression that applies only to the original finest child, such as indexed Lines topology or image labels, no longer disables additive streaming ladders on safe synthesized gsplat levels.

#### Keep the 4D spiral example practical to generate

The temporal spiral sphere now uses a representative animation-sized point set
instead of materialising more than 100 million point records, so
``make run-examples`` can complete without exhausting host memory.

#### Honor Cache Overrides for Line Admission

The `SceneLoader`'s session-scoped eager line-admission gate is now sized from
the same resolved cache pool the cache tiers use — explicit cache-pool override,
measured heap, device class, then fixed fallback — instead of the measured heap
alone. Safari and the native WKWebView launcher (no `performance.memory`) are
therefore no longer pinned to a 256 MiB line budget when a larger session budget
is configured with `?cacheBudgetMB=` or `LUXAR_CACHE_BUDGET_MB`.

#### Keep unrelated Playwright specs runnable with stale examples

The Playwright pre-flight now warns instead of aborting the whole run when
example datasets are stale. Specs using the shared page fixture repeat the
rebuild guidance beside a failure, while example-independent coverage remains
available without waiting for the full example corpus to regenerate.

#### Refuse topology-changing indexed Lines ladders

Plain `add_lines(..., line_type="indexed", additive_lod=...)` calls now raise
when a multi-level additive ladder would replace the authored edge list with
invented per-component chains. Indexed components that already consist of
consecutive vertex pairs remain ladderable and round-trip their edges unchanged;
requests that resolve to a flat node preserve the authored edge list as before.

#### Viewer fixtures now track their producer's import closure

The viewer's generated-fixture freshness gate now fingerprints each fixture
producer and its reachable local Python imports through the same shared resolver
used by demos and examples. Unrelated Luxar source edits no longer force the
full fixture corpus to regenerate, and the obsolete package-wide production
fingerprint has been removed.

#### Stop progressive refinement when a pass cannot advance

The viewer now releases the scene update lock when a successful progressive LOD pass leaves every pending node at the same rung. The warning identifies each stalled node and its loaded/total rung count, while failed and aborted attempts retain their existing retry behavior.

#### Restructured demo archives cut the hosted payload nearly in half (#2333)

Rebuilt additive ladders and hosting-oriented chunks reduce the affected Zenodo
draft payloads from 2.17 GB to 1.28 GB without changing finest-level splats or
reconstruction measurements. The default 51-frame h2afva timelapse archive is
now 1.12 GB, reducing its advertised download requirement from 1787 MB to
1064 MB. The Milky Way dust archive also remains on its levels-preserving
generation.

#### The Visible Human colours and the CT organ labels now live inside their fits

Both hosted archives carry their per-splat payload as a native gsplat attribute
instead of alongside a positional `.npz`: `vh_head` as `colors`, `ct_atlas` as
the exact categorical `label_ids` channel. Those sidecars had no positions, so
each was only correct while its row order happened to match its store's, and
both fell out of order twice — once sampled before the writer's spatial reorder
(#1670), and again when the archives were restructured underneath them (#2334),
leaving the shipped pairs agreeing on 0.7% and 37% of splats. A native attribute
is permuted in lockstep with the centers, so the two cannot separate and the
`_colors_match_fit` / `_labels_match_fit` guards have nothing left to compare on
that path.

The 37% is the one worth dwelling on. Organs are large and spatially contiguous,
so a misindexed label attach still lands roughly a third of splats in the right
organ and renders plausible-looking anatomy with the rest silently mislabelled —
whereas vh_head's 0.7% looks obviously broken. Neither is caught by looking; both
were caught by the guards. That asymmetry is why the label channel is exact by
contract: an amplitude-style encoder would renumber organs, returning class 51 as
50 or 52 and attributing splats to the wrong anatomy with no error anywhere, so
the round trip is asserted for per-class populations, not just for a range.

Both payloads were attached to the PREVIOUS generation of each fit, before the
first save — the generation their pinned bytes pair with at agreement 1.000. No
re-sampling was involved, which matters because the acceptance gate cannot
validate a re-sample: splats sharing a voxel share an index in any coordinate
frame, so a re-sample taken with the wrong crop box also scores 1.000, and #1670
needed three separate out-of-band checks to trust one. The provenance here is the
same bytes those checks already cleared.

The two-pass sampling on the refit paths stays, for a reason unrelated to
ordering. `sample_colors` and `sample_labels` round to the nearest voxel while the
writer quantizes centers, so a splat within a quantization step of a rounding
boundary changes voxel across a save. Attaching in a single pass mislabels exactly
those — 2 of 6000 on the vh_head fixture, each within 6.2e-05 of a boundary
against a 1.2e-04 quantization step. Invisible on screen, but it drops a fresh
pair from agreement 1.000 to 0.9993, and the thresholds are calibrated against an
exact 1.000 baseline. So both demos save, sample at the stored centers, attach,
and save again.

The sidecars are not gone. Each in-repo Git-LFS payload is a different generation
with no payload channel, and is still what a checkout resolves first, so both
demos prefer the native attribute and fall back to the sidecar for a fit that has
none. They retire together with those payloads (#2354). The hosted sidecars were
re-exported from the new archives' own channels, which is what let each
positional pair move atomically as the manifest generator requires — and makes
them aligned by construction rather than by a measurement that happened to pass.

`ct_atlas` also got smaller on the way through: 10.1 MB to 7.0 MB.

#### Keep positional demo payloads on one generation (#2338)

The demo-data resolver now rejects mixed current and superseded fit/sidecar pairs, while preserving a complete prior generation when no current replacement exists.

#### Demo archive rebuilds recover their recorded pipelines (#2340)

The h2afva stack, h2afva timelapse, and two-channel neuromast demos now carry
reproducible recompute paths for their shipped archives. The reusable
`luxar.gsplats.restride` helper performs memory-bounded stacked-axis subsampling
while preserving partition, LOD, and painter-order metadata.

Zipped archive characteristic discovery now identifies standalone gsplat stores
from their format metadata instead of archive member order, while refusing to
mistake a gsplat node nested inside a Luxar scene for a complete fit archive.

#### Guard positional-pair generation identity (#2342)

Manifest checks now pin positional-pair hosted digests with their history depths, require uncommitted re-pins to preserve prior cache digests in the runtime-readable fallback slot, and deep-check locatable current hosted pairs before publication.

#### Visible Human cold fetch now verifies the path users take (#2343)

The Visible Human demo now resolves its fit and positional colors sidecar through
the manifest-backed loader instead of hand-copying cache and Git LFS files. Cold
fetch verification therefore covers the demo's real path, enforces both pinned
digests, and cannot green-light payload removal while users would still fall back
to the 1.1 GB source download and GPU refit.

#### Route hosted demo inputs through the manifest (#2346)

The DESI galaxies, CELLxGENE Census UMAP, and human and mouse multiome peak UMAP demos now resolve their hosted inputs through the checksum-verified dataset manifest instead of reading packaged files directly. DESI retains its source-catalog rebuild fallback when the precomputed scene is unavailable, and `CENSUS_UMAP_CACHE` still accepts an explicit custom cache. The Census demo now exits non-zero, after printing its regeneration guidance, when the default coordinates cache cannot be resolved.

#### Zenodo characteristic refreshes stop reporting unreadable archives as success (#2350)

`gen_zenodo_records.py --refresh` now writes every successful measurement before reporting pinned fit archives it could not read and exiting non-zero. Unreadable copies whose bytes do not match the pin are counted separately without failing, while non-fit companion files are ignored. Explicit `--archives-root` runs report how many archive candidates were selected from that staging tree and warn when none matched, including the namespaced layout the command expects.

#### Explain unavailable h2afva quality figures

The Zenodo record now explains why neither published h2afva timelapse archive has a reconstruction-quality figure and records that the 51-frame archive is a strided slice of the same fit. The record check accepts an absent PSNR only when the row carries a reader-facing quality caveat, so future unexplained gaps still fail validation.

#### Stream `gsplat flatten` without materializing the full tree

`luxar gsplat flatten` now reads one default-selected leaf at a time and stages
the flat output on disk, removing the whole-tree load and concatenation that
made large partitioned stores run out of memory. The command requires precision
encoding; this preserves the bounded-memory write but produces larger output
than the previous auto-encoded default. Stacked categorical axes remain grouped
globally so per-timepoint chunk reads retain the locality of the in-memory path.

#### Diagnose unreadable pinned fits during Zenodo checks

`gen_zenodo_records.py --check` now distinguishes a manifest-pinned fit archive that is present but unparsable from an archive absent from the machine, reports the affected path, and exits non-zero. Archive candidates that cannot be read at all are reported separately with permissions advice instead of fetch advice.

#### Zenodo records measure the archive generation they serve

When more than one local copy of a demo archive exists, the Zenodo record
generator now measures the copy matching the manifest pin instead of whichever
copy appears first. This prevents stale repo bytes from supplying published
figures or hiding a readable pinned cache copy, while retaining the first local
copy that can be read as the pre-refresh fallback when the pinned generation is
not present.

#### Off-screen partition parts stop loading

The viewer now applies a frustum-only selector to spatial partition groups, so
parts outside the camera stop fetching and become eligible for eviction while
all in-frustum parts continue rendering together. Parts are resynchronized when
they re-enter the view, and footprint-expanded geometry bounds prevent visible
point, line, and Gaussian-splat edges from being culled early.

#### Drosophila timelapse rebuilds preserve their recorded pipeline (#2367)

The 500-timepoint Drosophila embryogenesis demo now provides a runnable
recompute path with source-contract checks, resumable fitting, the published
fixed amplitude cutoff, and validation against the recorded archive topology
and splat counts.

#### Zenodo refresh distinguishes inaccessible archives from absent ones (#2368)

`gen_zenodo_records.py --refresh` now reports fit archive candidates that cannot
be opened for hashing, including a failed candidate before a readable fallback,
instead of treating them as absent. Committed measurements remain counted as
preserved, and unverified bytes remain non-failing because they cannot be
checked against the manifest pin. The same hash-failure diagnostic now applies
to `--check`, including when another local candidate can still be hashed.

#### Additive LOD ladders are visible in the viewer debug surface (#2373)

`window.__luxarDebug` now reports bounded per-level additive load timings,
per-node committed ladder depth and quality, the adaptive-DPR healthy-cadence
estimate plus whether its sampler is active, and SliceCache ladder-depth/fullness
statistics. Mesh reveal ladders also show residency in the data monitor's
scene-graph row. This makes nD playback quality and cache convergence directly
observable without reconstructing them from raw element counts or renderer pass
counters; the cadence estimate rejects isolated stalls and is not perceived FPS.

#### Give a sliced node's additive ladder a share of the frame, not a byte budget

`stream_ladder` derived its first rung from a download budget — 39,062 elements
for 200 ms at 25 Mbps — and applied it to the node's TOTAL element count. But the
viewer draws one hidden-axis coordinate at a time, so on a sliced nD node that
rung arrives divided by the number of stops. Measured per resident slice:
human_multiome 6,510 of 1,041,455 (0.63%), zebrahub 5,580 of 640,830 (0.87%),
cellxgene 1.30%, mouse and ESM3 3.39%, and arxiv 0.59%.

Above one slice the first rung is now floored at `n / SLICED_LADDER_MAX_DEPTH`,
giving every accepted sliced leaf **12.5% of its mean resident slice** at first
paint:

| demo | slices | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| human_multiome | 6 | 0.63% | 12.50% |
| zebrahub | 7 | 0.87% | 12.50% |
| cellxgene_census | 3 | 1.30% | 12.50% |
| mouse_multiome | 6 | 3.39% | 12.50% |
| esm3_protein | 2 | 3.39% | 12.50% |
| arxiv_papers | 2 | 0.59% | 12.50% |

A share rather than a byte budget because a share is what predicts whether the
opening frame is recognisable: 0.03% renders blank (a 500-timepoint demo, decoded
and confirmed against playback at 20-51 splats), 12.5% is soft but usable
(neuromast, 110,614 measured at rest against a 113,947 metadata mean), and 54% is
fine on only 1,735 absolute elements — which is what rules out an absolute floor.
The latency cost is accepted rather than hidden:
first paint moves from ~200 ms to ~123-2,100 ms, with the upper end from arxiv's
two-stop shape. Part of that is repaid in requests, since hosted first paint is
dominated by request count and fewer, fatter rungs mean fewer nodes to fetch.

Three properties worth knowing. The floor needs no slice term — requiring
`rung0/S >= share * (n/S)` cancels to `rung0 >= share * n` — so it is
slice-invariant and a demo that gains a dimension cannot silently regress. It is a
`max()`, so a node whose budget rung already clears the share keeps its finer
ladder, and an unsliced node is untouched entirely. And the 12.5% is an
**aggregate**: rung 0 is a prefix of a global ordering, so it concentrates where
the signal is rather than spreading in proportion to slice size, and on a
non-uniform hidden axis the sparsest stops get less. Measured on a published
500-timepoint demo, `additive_0` is a median of 45 splats per timepoint but p05 =
7 and min = 1, against 41.7 predicted by a uniform assumption. A 2-7 stop
categorical axis has little room to be non-uniform, which is what this was sized
for; a long timelapse wants its per-stop histogram checked instead.

The 900,000-element commit ceiling is still authoritative. A sliced leaf above
7.2 million elements cannot deliver a 12.5% first rung safely, so
`stream_ladder` rejects it and asks the author to partition after moving any
stacked axis last, or to supply explicit capped cuts, rather than silently
